titleEn: Decoding cosmic "voids": one of the most mysterious structures in the universe
summaryEn: Looking up at the night sky, it is easy to feel that the universe is packed with stars and galaxies. In reality the opposite is true: most of the universe's volume consists of almost empty regions where matter is extremely sparse. Astronomers call these regions cosmic voids. Intriguingly, it is these regions of "nothing" that take up most of the space in the universe.
